programs.name: logisticfit
programs.purpose: Estimate logistic growth parameters from binary time and population values.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: LOGISTICFIT - least squares fit of a LOGISTIC function to input data

params.name: n
params.description: Number of time values and population values.

params.name: nstart
params.description: First index in the input window.

params.name: nend
params.description: Exclusive end index of the input window.

params.name: outpar
params.description: File receiving the ASCII fit results.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Finite differences and linear regressions use float arithmetic; K is rounded with NINT, and the second fit uses log. Zero denominators, invalid logarithms, short input, or windows shorter than two samples can produce invalid results or undefined behavior. The population read has no upper window bound: a complete input with nend<n writes past the allocated population array. Missing input leaves allocated values uninitialized.
programs.difficulty_reason: The two regression passes and finite differences require careful numerical and edge-case reproduction.

test_cases.description: Fit eight positive generated samples and write results to stdout.
test_cases.command: (lorenz stepmax=8 mode=x h=0.1; sird_epidemic stepmax=8 mode=I h=0.1) | logisticfit n=8 outpar=/dev/stdout

test_cases.description: Fit a shortened input window while avoiding the population buffer overrun.
test_cases.command: (lorenz stepmax=8 mode=x h=0.1; sird_epidemic stepmax=6 mode=I h=0.1) | logisticfit n=8 nstart=2 nend=8 outpar=/dev/stdout

programs.name: lorenz
programs.purpose: Integrate the Lorenz equations and output selected attractor coordinates.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output xy, yz, xz, xyz, x, y, or z.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive Runge-Kutta-England solver evolves doubles, then converts each output to float; chaotic trajectories amplify numerical differences and adaptive step decisions.
programs.difficulty_reason: It depends on an adaptive iterative ODE solver and a chaotic system.

test_cases.command: lorenz stepmax=32 mode=xyz h=0.02 rho=25 sigma=9 eta=2 > lorenz_xyz.bin

test_cases.description: Output one coordinate with altered initial conditions and tolerance.
test_cases.command: lorenz stepmax=32 mode=z y0=2 y1=1 y2=3 tol=1e-7 > lorenz_z.bin

programs.name: rossler
programs.purpose: Integrate the Rossler equations and output selected attractor coordinates.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output xy, yz, xz, xyz, x, y, or z.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive Runge-Kutta-England solver evolves doubles, then converts each output to float; chaotic trajectories amplify numerical differences and adaptive step decisions.
programs.difficulty_reason: It depends on an adaptive iterative ODE solver and a chaotic system.

test_cases.description: Output a short three-coordinate trajectory with changed coefficients.
test_cases.command: rossler stepmax=32 mode=xyz h=0.02 a=0.1 b=0.3 c=4 > rossler_xyz.bin

test_cases.description: Output one coordinate with altered initial conditions and tolerance.
test_cases.command: rossler stepmax=32 mode=y y0=2 y1=1 y2=3 tol=1e-7 > rossler_y.bin

programs.name: seir_epidemic
programs.purpose: Integrate a susceptible, exposed, infected, and removed epidemic model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SEIREPIDEMIC - the SEIR and SEIRS EPIDEMIC models

params.name: normalize
params.description: Divide initial populations by N when nonzero.

params.name: scale
params.description: Output scaling: 0 none, 1 by N, 2 by s0.

params.name: e0
params.description: Read but never used to initialize the exposed state.

params.name: i0
params.description: Assigned to the exposed state; the infected state starts at zero.

params.name: k
params.description: Removal rate; selfdoc instead describes this as transmission.

params.name: eti
params.description: Exposure-to-infection rate when omitted. When supplied, it is read into k and eti remains zero; k is then overwritten by its own parameter or default.

params.name: b
params.description: Exposure rate; selfdoc instead describes this as removal.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output all four series or S, E, I, or R.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive solver uses double state, converts output to float, and applies scaling in float. Initial exposed and infected values and the eti parameter have the assignment defects described above. Nonzero scale values other than 1 or 2 multiply output by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The model uses an adaptive iterative solver with multiple state variables and source-specific parameter defects.

test_cases.description: Output all compartments with scaling and vital dynamics.
test_cases.command: seir_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.25 N=200 i0=2 scale=1 mu=0.001 nu=0.002 xi=0.01 mode=SEIR > seir_all.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise the supplied eti behavior and single-compartment output.
test_cases.command: seir_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.1 eti=0.2 b=0.4 k=0.3 mode=E scale=2 > seir_e.bin

programs.name: sir_epidemic
programs.purpose: Integrate a susceptible, infected, and removed epidemic model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SIR_EPIDEMIC - the SIR and SIRS EPIDEMIC models with and without

params.name: normalize
params.description: Divide initial populations by N when nonzero.

params.name: scale
params.description: Output scaling: 0 none, 1 by N, 2 by s0.

params.name: k
params.description: Removal rate; selfdoc instead describes this as transmission.

params.name: b
params.description: Infection rate; selfdoc instead describes this as removal.

params.name: nu
params.description: Documented death rate, but never read from parameters; the code always uses zero.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output SIR, S, or R; documented I is rejected because the source checks S twice.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive solver uses double state, converts output to float, and applies scaling in float. The documented nu parameter is ignored and mode=I errors. Nonzero scale values other than 1 or 2 multiply output by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The model uses an adaptive iterative solver with multiple state variables and source-specific parameter defects.

test_cases.description: Output all compartments with social distancing and reinfection.
test_cases.command: sir_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.25 N=200 i0=2 b=0.6 k=0.2 gamma=5 xi=0.01 scale=1 mode=SIR > sir_all.bin
sir_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.1 normalize=0 N=10 s0=9 i0=1 b=0.02 k=0.3 mode=R > sir_r.bin

programs.name: sird_epidemic
programs.purpose: Integrate a susceptible, infected, recovered, and dead epidemic model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SIRD_EPIDEMIC - the SIRD and SIRDS EPIDEMIC models

params.name: normalize
params.description: Divide initial populations by N when nonzero.

params.name: scale
params.description: Output scaling: 0 none, 1 by N, 2 by s0.

params.name: k
params.description: Recovery rate; selfdoc instead describes this as transmission.

params.name: b
params.description: Infection rate; selfdoc instead describes this as removal.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output all four series or S, I, R, or D.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive solver uses double state, converts output to float, and applies scaling in float. Nonzero scale values other than 1 or 2 multiply output by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The model uses an adaptive iterative solver with four coupled state variables.

test_cases.description: Output all compartments with mortality and social distancing.
test_cases.command: sird_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.25 N=200 i0=2 b=0.6 k=0.2 nu=0.05 gamma=5 scale=1 mode=SIRD > sird_all.bin

test_cases.description: Output deaths without normalization and with s0 scaling.
test_cases.command: sird_epidemic stepmax=32 h=0.1 normalize=0 N=10 s0=9 i0=1 d0=0 b=0.02 nu=0.1 scale=2 mode=D > sird_d.bin
